title: Minimum Number of Valid Strings to Form Target II
summary: Given an array of strings words and a string target, determine the least number of strings from words that can be concatenated to form target.
statement: Given an array of strings words and a string target, determine the least number of strings from words that can be concatenated to form target. If target cannot be formed, return -1. A string is valid if it is a prefix of any string in words.
constraints: words contains at most 100 lowercase strings with total length at most 100,000; target length is at most 50,000.
Any nonempty prefix of any word may be appended, and prefixes may be reused.
Return the minimum number of valid prefixes forming target exactly, or -1.
hints: At each target position, only the longest matching dictionary prefix matters because every shorter prefix is also valid.
Compute exact word-versus-target LCP lengths with Z arrays, then treat each position as an interval reach.
Greedily take a new piece when the current frontier ends, extending to the farthest reachable endpoint.
The Z values are collision-free, and the standard minimum-jump exchange argument proves each frontier choice optimal.
editorial: The Z values are collision-free, and the standard minimum-jump exchange argument proves each frontier choice optimal.

tests.explanation: The target splits into aa, bcd, and abc, so three prefixes suffice.
Two copies of prefix ababa form the target.
